sections.h2: Selling in Derry Township and Hershey
sections.html:
Derry Township is the municipality that contains Hershey. A sale there is shaped by a stable local economy built around chocolate, tourism and a major medical center, and by a tax setup that runs through Dauphin County rather than a local collector. The township sits in southeastern Dauphin County, east of Harrisburg, with Lebanon County on its eastern edge. When people say they live in Hershey, their deed usually says Derry Township. The unincorporated communities inside it include Hershey, Palmdale, Swatara, Hockersville, Oakmont, Waltonville and part of Stoverdale.

A seller here should line up four things: who bills the taxes, what transfer tax applies, how assessments and appeals work in Dauphin County, and what the township's Community Development office handles.

The population estimate is 25,179 for July 1, 2025, only slightly above the 2010 count of 24,679, so this is a mature community that grows slowly. Nearly one in five residents is 65 or older. Hersheypark and other attractions are run by Hershey Entertainment and Resorts, and the township levies an amusement tax tied to them.

sections.h2: Who bills property tax and at what rates
sections.html:
Since January 1, 2023, the Dauphin County Treasurer's Office collects both township and Derry Township School District real estate taxes. The township's Tax Association Office closed that day, and occupation and local services taxes moved to Keystone Collections Group.

The township's tax page lists these real estate millage rates: 2.53810 mills for the township, 20.3387 mills for the school district and 9.193 mills for Dauphin County. Rates change when budgets are approved, so call the county treasurer for the current numbers before you build a net sheet.

Other township taxes depend on the person, not the house. Earned income tax is 1 percent, split evenly between the township and the school district, and the township also receives $250 from each employed resident earning over $12,000. A buyer moving into Derry will pay those, but they do not affect your proceeds.

sections.h2: Transfer tax on a Derry Township sale
sections.html:
The total is 2 percent of the sale price. The state's Department of Revenue receives 1 percent, and the municipality and the school district each receive half of one percent, so the township's share is 0.5 percent of the purchase price. The Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds collects it at recording.

The sales agreement determines which side pays, and the state holds both parties responsible. Transfers between spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, and siblings are generally exempt. For other exemptions, the Dauphin recorder suggests checking with an attorney or the Department of Revenue.

The Recorder of Deeds is at the Dauphin County Courthouse in Harrisburg, and its records begin in 1785. Fees for recording are set by the state legislature.

The Dauphin County Office of Tax Assessment values real property, keeps ownership records and runs the county's homestead and farmstead exclusion, its Clean and Green preferential assessment program and its tax deferral program. Its office is on the second floor of the County Administration Building at 2 South Second Street in Harrisburg, and its parcel data is online.

The office does not set tax rates. The county, the township and the school district do that after assessments are in. If you think your assessment is too high, ask the office for the appeal rules and the filing date that applies to your parcel.

Act 29 of 2026 creates a county-kept contact registry for properties that are not owner-occupied. Owners, and lenders after a foreclosure, must give the county a name, address, phone and email for someone authorized to resolve code violations, within 30 days of taking ownership and within 30 days of any change. A failure to comply can bring a $500 fine, and owner-occupied principal residences are exempt.

If you are selling a rental, your buyer takes on that duty at closing, so mention it. If you stay on as the contact until closing, keep your details current with the county.

sections.h2: What the township's Community Development office handles
sections.html:
The township municipal complex at 600 Clearwater Road in Hershey is where you ask about permits, zoning and any open code issue on an address. Do that before you list, because a buyer's lender or inspector may ask for the same paperwork.

  • Check whether any past work on the house, such as a finished basement, a deck or a pool, had a permit
  • Ask which zoning district the lot is in if your buyer plans a business, an addition or a rental
  • Confirm that street light assessments and other township charges on the account are current
  • Sign up for the township's eNews to follow notices that affect your street

A little time spent on these items before you list keeps surprises away from the closing table.

1. Call the Dauphin County Treasurer for balances on township and school taxes.
  2. Ask Community Development about permits and open code issues.
  3. Check street light assessments and other township charges.
  4. Ask the Office of Tax Assessment about the exclusion or program on the parcel.
  5. Decide who pays the 2 percent transfer tax in the agreement of sale.

With a median home value near $390,000 and strong local employers, a house in good order can sell through a normal listing. An as-is sale makes more sense when you are settling an estate, relocating, or facing repairs you would rather not finance.

Whichever path you choose, ask for the net figure in writing: price, less the 2 percent transfer tax if you agree to pay it, payoffs, prorated county, township and school taxes, and any repair credit. Request the buyer's proof of funds and closing date before you take the house off the market.

faqs.q: Is Hershey a separate town from Derry Township?
faqs.a: No. Hershey is an unincorporated community inside Derry Township, so deeds, permits and taxes for a Hershey address go through the township and Dauphin County.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a house sale in Derry Township?
faqs.a: It totals 2 percent: 1 percent to the state, 0.5 percent to the township and 0.5 percent to the school district, collected by the Dauphin County Recorder of Deeds.

faqs.q: Who collects real estate taxes on a Derry Township house?
faqs.a: The Dauphin County Treasurer's Office collects both township and school district real estate taxes. Call the treasurer for balances before closing.

faqs.q: Do I need to register a rental house I am selling in Dauphin County?
faqs.a: Act 29 of 2026 requires owners of non-owner-occupied property to give the county contact details, with updates within 30 days of any change. Your buyer takes on that duty when they become the owner.

faqs.q: Are family transfers exempt from realty transfer tax in Dauphin County?
faqs.a: Transfers between spouses, parents and children, grandparents and grandchildren, and siblings are generally exempt, though other exemptions exist. Confirm with an attorney or the Department of Revenue.
